newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends sharply up as China worries ease.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends sharply up as China worries ease.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply higher against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday, rebounding on defence ministry assurances that no signs of impending major war games in rival China had been detected, dealers said.
The local unit, which tumbled on Monday on worries of new frictions with Taiwan's arch adversary across the Taiwan strait, ended Tuesday's trading at T$27.565 against Monday's T$27.625 close.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$381.5 million.

The local currency had plunged T$0.08 on Monday along with the stock market following an unconfirmed news report that China was planning to mount war games to protest a Taiwan visit by Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama.
Taiwan's defence ministry said late Monday it had detected no major military movements from China or signs that war games were in the works, and reiterated the denial on Tuesday.
"The assurance attracted bargain hunters who bought up the Taiwan dollar, thinking the rate would eventually settle back to the T$27.5 level," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Before Monday's tumble, the Taiwan dollar had stalemated at or near T$27.5 for months, with any fall or rise quickly countered by a corresponding swing in the other direction.
Dealers added they did not expect the recent export ban on pork exports following a hog foot and month disease outbreak to influence the rate significantly.
"Investors have calmed down, and now they realise the pork industry is pretty small compared to the other export sectors," said another dealer.
A T$27.52-60 range was seen for Wednesday.
